transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

At nine years old, a washing machine is near or past its typical lifespan, so repair costs often outweigh the value of a new unit. It depends on whether you can find an affordable replacement and if the specific fault is cheap to fix compared to buying new. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the water-level sensing or the control side. With the machine switched off does the drum turn freely by hand, and is all the water gone before it tries to spin?
With the power off, the drum turns freely by hand and quietly, with no scraping or rumble. And yes, the water all drains away fine before it would normally try to spin.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is the drive belt. Let's see whether the machine itself can spin: take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. Does it spin up properly when it's empty?

I ran it empty as you suggested and the drum doesn't spin at all, I just hear the relays click and nothing else. No motor noise whatsoever. I should say the belt would be my guess too, but I haven't looked at it yet.

A washing machine won't run if the door lock doesn't engage. Close the door firmly, check nothing like a sock or the seal is caught in it, and start a programme. Does the door click locked and the lock light come on?

The door locks fine and the lock light behaves normally, and the pump and controls respond. It's only the drum that never turns. Sometimes a light flashes after a long wait. Is there something else I should check?

Yes, you should check if the drive belt is intact and properly fitted on the motor pulley. If your model uses a direct drive motor, the issue may lie with the carbon brushes or the motor itself. It's also worth checking the settings: wool, delicate and hand-wash programmes spin very gently, and options such as "no spin", "rinse hold" or a low spin speed stop the final spin. Was a normal programme with a normal spin speed selected, or was one of those options set?

I don't think the settings are the cause, because the drum doesn't turn during the wash either, not just the spin. I should also mention that a few weeks ago I noticed a faint hot electrical smell from the machine, though not since. Before this it had been a bit erratic, sometimes slow to start turning. How do I check the belt and motor safely?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. You cannot safely inspect the internal belt or motor without first disconnecting the washing machine from the mains power supply. Accessing these components requires removing the rear panel, which should only be done by a qualified technician due to electrical safety risks. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
